home.metaTitle: Drought early warning for the Choke Mountain Watershed
home.heroTitle: Know the season before you plant it.
home.heroLead: AI-DREWS turns satellite rainfall, reanalysis and the Pacific El Niño signal into a drought forecast for each cell of an 18,948 km² catchment — then into advice a smallholder can act on, in their own language.
home.ctaNote: Institutions request an account. Farmers can sign up and a development agent confirms them.

catchment.label: Surveyed catchment
catchment.note: Real Choke boundary, not a bounding box

home.whyTitle: A forecast is only useful if it reaches the field in time.
home.whyLead: Drought in the Ethiopian highlands is survivable when it is known early. The gap has never been the science — it is the distance between a model and a farmer deciding what to sow.

warning.title: Early warning, per cell
warning.body: Drought probability for each grid cell of the catchment, with the observed Sc-PDSI for the ground as it is now.

decision.title: Advice, not just numbers
decision.body: Crop, planting window, water management and preparedness, chosen by rule from the forecast and the crop in that field.

reach.title: Reaches a feature phone
reach.body: The same answers through the app, an SMS or USSD menu, and an extension agent — not only to farmers with smartphones.

home.howLead: Four steps, each one auditable: every figure in the interface traces back to the run and the dataset that produced it.

observe.title: Observe
observe.body: CHIRPS rainfall, ERA5 reanalysis and NOAA Niño 3.4, ingested with a manifest recording where each value came from.

model.title: Model
model.body: SPI-3, VCI and a self-calibrating Palmer index feed a hybrid network that forecasts drought a month ahead.

advise.title: Advise
advise.body: Published rules turn probability and crop into a recommendation, with traditional indicators weighed alongside the model.

deliver.title: Deliver
deliver.body: Dashboards for institutions, a plot-level page for farmers, and the 977 hotline for a phone with no app.

home.howMore: The data and the models in detail
home.modelsTitle: Three models, and what each is actually good for.
home.modelsLead: Performance is published rather than implied. These are the figures from the trained artefacts currently in service.

drought.title: Seasonal drought
drought.body: A CNN reads the spatial field, an LSTM the history, and a Fourier branch the seasonal cycle. It predicts the chance of drought for each cell.

enso.title: El Niño outlook
enso.body: Forecasts the Niño 3.4 index up to a year ahead — and keeps persistence wherever the network cannot beat it by a clear margin.

yield.title: Crop yield
yield.body: Gradient-boosted trees relating rainfall, the ENSO phase and the previous seasons to yield for tef, wheat and maize.

home.modelsCaveat: Honest limits: the drought model is skilful one month ahead. Two- and three-month views are shown for context and should not be planted on. The El Niño model keeps persistence at leads where it cannot beat it.
home.whoTitle: One forecast, six kinds of decision.
home.whoLead: The same catchment model, priced and presented for the decision each group actually makes.

howItWorks.title: From satellite rainfall to a planting decision.
howItWorks.lead: What the platform observes, what it models, what it is skilful at — and what it is not.
howItWorks.dataTitle: Four public datasets, and nothing proprietary.
howItWorks.dataLead: Each ingest writes a manifest recording the source, the window and the checksum, so any figure in the interface can be traced to the file it came from.

source.csa: Crop statistics for tef, wheat and maize

feeds.balance: The Sc-PDSI water balance and PET
feeds.enso: The ENSO phase and its forecast

howItWorks.dataNote: ERA5 is checked against CHIRPS and station records rather than trusted outright; where they disagree the disagreement is recorded instead of smoothed away.

observe.title: Ingest and validate
observe.body: Rainfall, reanalysis and the ENSO index are pulled on a schedule, checked for gaps and range, and written with a manifest. A failed check stops the run rather than publishing a gap as a zero.

model.title: Indices and forecast
model.body: SPI-3 is fitted per cell against a gamma distribution, VCI from vegetation condition, and Sc-PDSI from a Thornthwaite water balance. A CNN-LSTM with a Fourier branch forecasts drought probability per cell.

advise.title: Rules, not generation
advise.body: A published rule table turns probability and crop into a recommendation. Nothing writes agronomic advice freely — the same inputs always produce the same guidance, and the rules version is recorded with every advisory.

deliver.title: Delivery
deliver.body: Institutions get dashboards and an API; farmers get their own plots, an assistant in three languages, and the 977 hotline for a phone with no app.

howItWorks.modelsLead: Figures taken from the trained artefacts, not from a paper.

drought.title: Seasonal drought
drought.body: A 2-D convolution over the grid, an LSTM over the history and a Fourier branch for the seasonal cycle, combined to a per-cell probability.

enso.title: El Niño outlook
enso.body: Trained on the full NOAA record. At each lead it is kept only where it beats persistence on validation by a clear margin.

yield.title: Crop yield
yield.body: Gradient-boosted trees over rainfall, ENSO phase and the previous seasons, fitted to CSA statistics for the three staples.

howItWorks.limitsLead: Stated here with the same prominence as the claims, because planting and procurement decisions are made on this.

lead.title: Skilful one month ahead
lead.body: The drought model is validated at a one-month lead. Two- and three-month views exist for context and should not be planted on.

persistence.title: Persistence is often the better answer
persistence.body: The ENSO model keeps persistence at any lead where the network cannot beat it by at least 5% on validation. Several leads are persistence.

yield.title: Yield is indicative
yield.body: Mean absolute percentage error is about 24%. It is useful for comparing seasons and crops, not for guaranteeing a harvest figure.

sms.title: The hotline is not connected
sms.body: The 977 pipeline is complete and tested, but no carrier carries it yet: that needs an Ethio Telecom short code and an aggregator contract.

howItWorks.rulesVersionNote: Every advisory records the rules version and the model run that produced it, so a recommendation given last season can still be reconstructed.

about.title: A drought early warning system built for one watershed, properly.
about.lead: AI-DREWS is a research and operations platform for the Choke Mountain Watershed in Amhara, Ethiopia, built by a team across four institutions.
about.story1: Continental drought products are too coarse for a decision made on a half-hectare plot. AI-DREWS models one catchment at a resolution a farmer can act on, using the real surveyed boundary rather than a rectangle drawn around it — 15 of the 64 grid cells fall outside the watershed and are excluded rather than quietly averaged in.
about.story2: The platform is operational as well as scientific: the same models that produce the research outputs serve the dashboards, the farmer advisories and the hotline, so the numbers in a paper and the numbers a development agent sees are the same numbers.
about.hostBody: Choke Mountain feeds the Blue Nile and supports dense smallholder agriculture across East Gojjam. It is where the system is calibrated and where it is deployed.
about.teamLead: Atmospheric physics, statistics, data science and engineering across four institutions.
about.contactNote: Direct contact details for the investigators are held in the project record rather than published here. Enquiries reach the team through an access request, which also leaves a record of what was asked.
about.talkTitle: Working on drought in the highlands?
about.talkLead: Institutions request an account and we respond with a plan for their segment. Farmers can sign up directly, and a development agent confirms the holding.
